raw.summary: CWE‑79 (Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation, aka XSS) is a high‑likelihood software weakness affecting web‑based applications. It occurs when user‑controllable input is placed into HTML output without proper encoding, enabling script injection that can bypass access controls and read application data. The profile highlights the weakness, its impact, and recommended mitigations.

findings.text: User‑controllable input is not properly neutralized before being placed in web page output, creating a cross‑site scripting (XSS) weakness (CWE‑79).
The likelihood of exploit for this weakness is rated as high.
Exploitation can lead to bypassing access‑control mechanisms and reading confidential application data.
XSS is a subset of the broader injection category (CWE‑74).

affected.text: Any web‑based application that renders user‑supplied data without appropriate output encoding is potentially affected.

actions.text: Adopt a vetted web framework or library that automatically encodes output to prevent XSS.
Implement explicit output encoding for all dynamic content using context‑appropriate encoders (HTML, JavaScript, URL, etc.).
Add a Content Security Policy (CSP) to mitigate the impact of any injected scripts.
Conduct regular security testing (static analysis, dynamic scanning, manual code review) to detect XSS injection points.
Train developers on secure coding practices for handling user input and output encoding.
